issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares a Pneumatic interface with methods raisePressure(int) and openValve(), but the solution implements Pneumatic with raisePressure(int) and releaseValve(). Additionally, the solution classes that implement Pneumatic (e.g., LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) provide openValve() implementations. This name/signature mismatch between the interface and its implementations will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct method name specified by the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Pneumatic interface with the UML/problem statement by declaring raisePressure(int) and openValve() (i.e., rename releaseValve() to openValve()). Update the interface in both template and solution and ensure all implementing classes override openValve() accordingly so implementations and interface signatures match.

issues.description: The Pneumatic interface method name for opening the valve is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement's UML declares openValve(), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares releaseValve() while the solution classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement openValve(). This mismatch breaks the conceptual mapping for students (which method to implement) and creates a compile-time/instructional confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic API name consistent. Either rename releaseValve() in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java to openValve() to match the UML and the implementing classes, or update the implementing classes to override releaseValve() instead. Align the template Pneumatic.java stub accordingly so problem statement, template and solution use the same method name.
